summary: Describes an allocation plan for IPv6 addresses used to test prototype IPv6 software, as used by the early test network. It is now historic, replaced by RFC 3701.

eli5.summary: Before the new internet addresses were ready for everyone, testers needed a play area. This explained how addresses were handed out inside it.

questions: what was the ipv6 testing address allocation
how did ipv6 testbeds allocate addresses
subtitle: How the 6bone testbed allocated experimental IPv6 addresses.

tldr.problem: Testing IPv6 software required a temporary address space separate from production networks.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns a specific range (TLA 0x1FFE) within the aggregatable global unicast format for IPv6 testing.
tldr.outcome: The 6bone testbed was able to test IPv6 technologies in real environments. This RFC is now historic, replaced by RFC 3701 which uses different address allocations.

today: RFC 2471 is Historic. It has been replaced by RFC 3701, which uses different address allocations for IPv6 testing.

sections.title: Testing IPv6 Addresses
sections.content:
RFC 2471 defines an allocation plan for IPv6 addresses used to test prototype IPv6 software. These addresses are temporary and will be reclaimed; any system using them must renumber in the future. They are not routable on the Internet outside of IPv6 testing environments.

The addresses fit within the aggregatable global unicast format, which organizes the address space for efficient routing. They can be assigned manually, with auto-configuration, or with DHCP.
sections.eli5: These were pretend internet addresses testers could use to try out new IPv6 software. They worked like real addresses but only on test networks.

sections.title: Address Format and Structure
sections.content:
The test addresses use the standard aggregatable format: 001 (format prefix) | 1FFE (Top-Level Aggregation ID) | NLA ID (32 bits) | SLA ID (16 bits) | Interface ID (64 bits). The TLA value 1FFE was assigned by IANA for 6bone testing under the IETF IPng Transition Working Group.

The NLA (Next-Level Aggregation) ID identifies transit networks and end-user sites within the 6bone topology. The SLA (Site-Level Aggregation) ID is managed by individual organizations to create local address hierarchies and identify subnets.
sections.eli5: The address is broken into parts: the first says it is a test address, the next picks the 6bone testbed, then the site, then the network, then the machine.

sections.title: Administration
sections.content: The TLA ID space is temporary and administered by the 6bone activity chair. Users of these addresses must expect to renumber at some point in the future. The RFC explicitly notes that this space is not for operational use and addresses will not be routable on the public Internet.
sections.eli5: One person runs the testbed and hands out the address chunks. Everyone knows these addresses will go away someday.
